Agreed on next steps: share playbook, schedule tech deep dive, and confirm target accounts.
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-29 15:00 PST | Duration: ~60 mins | Attendees: Avery Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Zara Chen (Redwood CSM), Karen Yates (Seacliff), Liam O'Connor (Seacliff), Priya Desai (Seacliff)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Avery): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, happy holidays, we'll try to keep this to an hour, agenda is quick pipeline review and next steps for the co-sell plays.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Karen): thanks, Avery, appreciate it. we've got a few folks on our side today — liam and priya — we'll jump in, want to make sure we align on the two pilots we talked about.
00:35 Speaker 3 (Liam): yeah hi all, quick context: Seacliff's Q1 push is focused on healthcare workflow automation and a fintech customer that needs improved chat/AI routing.
00:48 Speaker 1 (Avery): perfect. miguel, mind kicking off with the tech checklist for the pilots?
01:02 Speaker 4 (Miguel): sure — quick caveat, transcript might be messy — but for the healthcare pilot we need SSO/SAML, SOC 2 compliance notes, data residency details, and the option for Private deployment or Dedicated capacity depending on the customer's security reqs. also, latency targets: under 300ms p95 for 2k concurrent users is what they asked for.
01:28 Speaker 3 (Liam): correct, that's their ask. cost is a concern — they asked about hosted vs dedicated pricing.
01:35 Speaker 4 (Miguel): right — we recommended starting hosted for speed, then move to Redwood Dedicated if they need predictability; for the healthcare client they might insist on VPC or on-prem later. we sent a rough TCO spreadsheet earlier but we'll share the partner pricing.
01:56 Speaker 2 (Karen): good. can you remind us of the fallback/failover story? iirc redwood has auto routing and model fallbacks?
02:06 Speaker 4 (Miguel): yes — smart routing across region/tier, automatic fallback to smaller model variants on capacity constraints. we also have KV/prefix caching to save cost on repeated queries. small note: sometimes the KV cache term gets garbled in docs, we call it "prefix cache" in the playbook.
02:24 Speaker 1 (Avery): on the commercial side we flagged 6 joint targets — priya, can you confirm which of these are ready for intro?
02:33 Speaker 5 (Priya): i have a list, three are ready for intro this quarter: two healthcare, one fintech. the other three need procurement cycles aligned.
02:45 Speaker 2 (Karen): okay that's inline. for the fintech one — regulatory wants KMS/HSM integration, are you able to support that?
02:56 Speaker 4 (Miguel): yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and there are HSM options for enterprise. we'll attach the security one-pager.
03:08 Speaker 5 (Priya): great. also, for onboarding, we need a small POC — 2 week pilot, with a 10k query seed set to validate latency and quality. can redwood do that on dedicated infra?
03:19 Speaker 4 (Miguel): we can spin up a dedicated pool for the POC, yes — but needs a commitment window; alternatively we can run a hosted POC with higher monitoring and a performance SLA for the trial. both are doable.
03:37 Speaker 1 (Avery): let's mark that as a deal-level decision — hig priority fintech pilot may require dedicated due to compliance.
03:45 Speaker 2 (Karen): agreed. moving on to deal reviews — we'll go through the top 6 briefly, call out blockers and champions.
03:53 Speaker 1 (Avery): Deal A (HealthSys) — stage: POC scoping — champion: Dr. Moore (CDO). status: Seacliff has intro, needs security docs and pricing. blocker: data residency and SOC 2 evidence.
04:12 Speaker 5 (Priya): we tried to upload initial questions but need a dedicated contact at Redwood for SOC 2 artifacts and architecture diagram.
04:22 Speaker 4 (Miguel): Zara will own sending the SOC 2 and architecture diagram, and i can do a short infra call.
04:33 Speaker 6 (Zara): i'll drop that in the shared folder after the call and cc priya.
04:40 Speaker 3 (Liam): Deal B (FinPay) — stage: discovery — champion: VP Eng (M. Alvarez). status: technical POC requested, regulatory needs KMS and SSO. blocker: pricing justification vs Anthropic solution they've benchmarked.
04:58 Speaker 4 (Miguel): on benchmarks, we did a small perf run last quarter that showed comparable latency and lower token cost with our batching + quantization suggestions; i'll pull that spreadsheet and share.
05:12 Speaker 3 (Liam): please do, that will help our economic case.
05:20 Speaker 1 (Avery): Deal C (MedEdge) — stage: committed pilot — champion: CIO — they want an on-prem option, 3 month pilot, legal needs indemnity language. blocker: procurement timeline overlaps Q2.
05:36 Speaker 2 (Karen): legal is going to be a modest obstacle but we've done private deployments with other partners. do you have a recent IA (integration agreement) template?
05:45 Speaker 4 (Miguel): yes, legal template and deployment runbook exist — i'll attach.
05:52 Speaker 1 (Avery): Deal D (RetailCo) — lower priority, stage: demo complete — champion: Head of Product. status: waiting on pricing.
06:03 Speaker 2 (Karen): Deal E (AutoTech) — intro stage, needs architecture diagram.
06:10 Speaker 1 (Avery): Deal F (CloudBank) — high priority — they want a canary rollout and A/B test with two models — also want per-token cost breakdown.
06:22 Speaker 4 (Miguel): we have per-route model dashboards in the Console; we can provide token-level cost and latency tracebacks — that tends to help finance.
06:33 Speaker 5 (Priya): ok thanks. on the partner ops side, we want a shared cadence — weekly sync is good, but can we also get a shared CRM tag or board so both teams can track joint touches?
06:45 Speaker 6 (Zara): yes, i'll create a shared board and tag the six accounts, and start logging touchpoints.
06:53 Speaker 1 (Avery): good. a couple things from the Redwood side — enablement deck and a short joint sell play. i'll share a link after the call.
07:02 Speaker 4 (Miguel): question from our side, any constraints on hosting region for these accounts?
07:09 Speaker 3 (Liam): HealthSys wants US-East only, FinPay wants EU residency for part of their datasets.
07:18 Speaker 4 (Miguel): noted. we support region pinning and private control plane options. i'll flag the need to validate EU data lanes for FinPay and probably suggest a dedicated EU pool.
07:30 Speaker 2 (Karen): on competitive positioning, FinPay ran a benchmark with Anthropic and liked the quality but cost was high; they asked if Redwood can provide a pricing model that shows break-even vs Anthropic at scale.
07:46 Speaker 4 (Miguel): we can — i'll create a cost model using batching and quant profiles; it'll show unit economics vs Anthropic and OpenAI for the same throughput.
07:57 Speaker 1 (Avery): we'll attach that with the pricing sheet.
08:05 Speaker 5 (Priya): for the confidentiality/contract asks, what's the typical turnaround time on redwood's legal review?
08:14 Speaker 6 (Zara): usually 2-3 weeks for standard terms, faster if we agree on a scoping addendum and limit exposures; enterprise SLA and SOC 2 docs are usually available immediately.
08:27 Speaker 3 (Liam): perfect. question: can we run a small accuracy eval on a representative prompt set during the POC? we want to baseline quality against their current vendor.
08:38 Speaker 4 (Miguel): absolutely — we can run prompt set evals, compare log-likelihoods and output quality. note: evals sometimes need human review for nuance; we recommend a 1-week labeled sample.
08:51 Speaker 5 (Priya): good. that'll help procurement justify the switch.
09:00 Speaker 1 (Avery): moving to responsibilities: Seacliff will own intro and initial stakeholder alignment, Redwood will own POC infra and security artifacts, and joint customer-facing demo scheduling. does that sound right?
09:13 Speaker 2 (Karen): yes.
09:16 Speaker 4 (Miguel): small tech note — for the healthcare pilot we should run a short model comparison: quantized 4-bit variant vs full FP16 to validate latency/quality tradeoffs. we'll propose model config in the tech-deep-dive.
09:31 Speaker 3 (Liam): okay that's fine, can you include cost delta in that doc?
09:36 Speaker 4 (Miguel): will do.
09:40 Speaker 1 (Avery): any other blockers?
09:43 Speaker 5 (Priya): procurement cycles might push MedEdge into Q2, but we'll try to accelerate.
09:50 Speaker 1 (Avery): ok — recap next steps: send playbook & pricing (Avery), share SOC2/arch + benchmark spreadsheet (Zara & Miguel), schedule technical deep-dive (Miguel), Seacliff to send target accounts (Karen/Priya).
10:05 Speaker 2 (Karen): i'll get the account list by next week.
10:10 Speaker 6 (Zara): i'll post SOC2 and architecture diagrams right after this call.
10:15 Speaker 4 (Miguel): i'll schedule the deep-dive with Priya and the infra team for the week of Jan 4.
10:22 Speaker 1 (Avery): great — we'll also set up the shared CRM board.
10:27 Speaker 5 (Priya): one last question — any thought on co-marketing for these logos if we close?
10:33 Speaker 1 (Avery): yes we'll draft a joint case study template but focus on pilots first.
10:38 Speaker 2 (Karen): thanks everyone — that was helpful.
10:42 Speaker 1 (Avery): thanks all, will follow up with notes. talk soon.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts: names sometimes garbled, timestamps approximated.
